title: Plucking Votes From Disasters
citation: Reeves, Andrew. 2004. "Plucking Votes From Disasters." Los Angeles Times, May 12.
card_summary: The article argues that U.S. presidents are more likely to grant federal disaster declarations to politically important states, especially battleground states, based on an analysis of disaster declarations from 1989 to 2003.
plain_english_summary: Presidents are more likely to approve disaster aid for states that are important in presidential elections, rather than just those with the greatest need.
research_question: Do presidential electoral considerations influence the granting of federal disaster declarations?
research_highlights: Presidents are more likely to grant disaster declarations to battleground states with more electoral votes, even after accounting for need.
More disaster declarations are granted during election years than in off years.
Need is still the best indicator, but electoral motivations play a dramatic role.
methods: Regression analysis of all disaster declarations from 1989 to 1999, with preliminary analysis through 2003.
Used insurance company figures, National Climatic Data Center damage declarations, and political significance of each state.
data_sources: National Climatic Data Center declarations of damage
Information about the political significance of each state
key_variables: State electoral importance (battleground status, electoral votes)
pull_quote: I found that the electoral motivations of the president -- Bush and his two predecessors -- had a dramatic effect on which states were granted disaster declarations.
